claims.text: Copper doping followed by tailored heat treatment will induce nanoscale copper-rich precipitates in the high-entropy alloy.
The induced copper-rich precipitates will enhance the alloy's heat-transfer capability.
Copper addition and precipitation will preserve the alloy's structural integrity.
The initial intermediate-layer alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution and lacks copper precipitates.
Such an alloy is currently used in plasma-facing reactor applications.
A tailored heat treatment can produce well-dispersed nanoscale copper precipitates.
The copper precipitates will form localized high-thermal-conductivity networks.
The high-entropy matrix will retain its strength and toughness after copper precipitation.
Copper has a higher intrinsic thermal conductivity than the constituent elements of the high-entropy alloy.
Copper-rich precipitates located along grain boundaries or within grains provide effective channels for phonon heat transfer.
The matrix's high-entropy configuration maintains resistance to deformation and thermal creep.
The copper-doped and heat-treated alloy will have higher thermal conductivity than the undoped control.
The thermal-conductivity increase will occur without a significant loss of yield strength or other structural-integrity indicators.
The predicted improvement will persist under high-temperature reactor conditions and representative mechanical loading.
Deviation from an optimal copper fraction could compromise heat-transfer enhancement and structural integrity.
Precipitate coarsening at excessive temperatures could compromise heat-transfer enhancement and structural integrity.
